name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +12 partisan lean
Incumbent Rick Larsen running with a large fundraising edge
Polymarket prices Larsen at 97% to win
Republican challenger Edwin Feller shows no meaningful financial support
model.rationale: The district's +12 Democratic lean, Larsen's incumbency and roughly $2 million in fundraising against a little-known, underfunded challenger, and prediction markets pricing Larsen near 97% all point to a comfortable incumbent win. No polls or expert ratings contradict this picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Feller or an unexpectedly favorable national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Larsen, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northwestern Washington district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. He has raised over $2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican challenger Edwin Feller has reported little fundraising and no significant outside support. Prediction markets give Larsen roughly a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Everything points to a safe Democratic hold, with Larsen favored by roughly twenty-two points. The main uncertainty is the width of the margin, not the winner.
